title: Suspect died of heart attack: Autopsy
article: Preliminary autopsy results show that a Vancouver man who died after a struggle with a police officer following a home invasion suffered a brain aneurysm and a heart attack.

Jeffrey Michael Berg, 37, died at Vancouver General Hospital Oct. 24 without regaining consciousness after collapsing two days earlier in a back lane close to a house which had been invaded in the 4800 block Slocan.

Berg was one of four men in a stolen getaway car that was rammed and immobilized by a police cruiser. He crawled through a smashed car window to confront the lone officer, who had been in the cruiser. The two struggled and Berg fell unconscious. His breathing stopped but was restarted by ambulance attendants when they reached the scene.
Results of tests to see whether Berg had taken drugs will not be available for a month. An inquest is to be held.
The officer who tackled Berg is now on routine leave. He will return to his regular job as a master dog handler this week.
Berg was "known to police in a minor way." Two of his three companions have been charged in the home invasion.
